title: General insurers clock 10.5% premium growth in October
summary: General insurance companies in India saw a 10.5% increase in gross direct premium income in October. Standalone health insurers also reported significant growth, outperforming general insurers in several areas. HDFC ERGO and SBI General led the performance among private insurers with impressive increases in premium income. Public sector insurers like National Insurance also experienced growth, though some faced declines.

title: Softbank further trims India exposure, offloads Meesho shares worth Rs 1,885 cr
summary: In the latest transaction, SVF II Meerkat (DE) LLC, an affiliate of SoftBank, offloaded 7.64 crore shares in Bengaluru-based Meesho, according to the block deal data on the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

title: Can markets extend gains amid rising crude and rate hike fears?
summary: The Indian stock indices experienced a retreat as increasing crude oil costs negatively impacted market sentiment. Retail inflation hit 6.09% in October, breaching the tolerance threshold set by the Reserve Bank of India. This spike raised alarms about possible future rate adjustments. Sectors like realty, auto, and cement faced considerable selling activity due to these economic dynamics. However, the benchmarks concluded the week with minor gains.

title: Can Indian IT stocks regain momentum as AI-led disruption reshapes the sector?
summary: The Indian IT sector has seen a rollercoaster of activity, where mid-sized companies have outperformed their larger peers recently. Increased deal bookings are promising, yet slow revenue growth due to client indecision lingers. The emergence of AI technology brings both new possibilities and pricing pressures for classic services. To sustain their margins in this shifting landscape, companies are honing their operational efficiency.

title: Dodging bullet loans hurt gold NBFCs after RBI’s revised lending rules trigger repayment stress
summary: Non-banking financial companies have begun reassessing gold loan structures following increased delinquencies in recent months. Bajaj Finance and Manappuram Finance are shifting towards longer-tenure loans in response to customer difficulties. Many borrowers are struggling to adapt to new repayment schedules that require more frequent payments. Muthoot Finance has also reported a significant rise in overdue loans tied to repayment structure changes.

title: ASA International set to exit India by year-end
summary: ASA International is in the process of exiting its India operations by the end of this year. The Reserve Bank of India approved the voluntary surrender of ASA's NBFC-MFI license for its India subsidiary. Financial difficulties and regulatory complexities have significantly impacted the company's operations in India since the Covid pandemic began. ASA has reported a reduction in its client base to approximately 9,000 after halting loan disbursals.

title: Coca-Cola CEO to visit India ahead of HCCH $1-billion listing
summary: Coca-Cola's CEO, Henrique Braun, is visiting India for three days to discuss the upcoming IPO of Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings. His schedule includes meetings with various stakeholders including bottling partners and bankers. The IPO is expected to reduce Coca-Cola's holding in HCCH from 60% to 45%. Additionally, India is emerging as a pivotal market for Coca-Cola amid increasing competition. The company's valuation is projected at around $10 billion following the IPO.

title: Warburg Pincus picks up Rs 1,663 crore stake in unit of Pricol
summary: Warburg Pincus will acquire a 38% stake in Pricol’s driver information and connected vehicle solutions business for ₹1,663 crore through its affiliate Topaz Terrace Investments. The business, which makes digital dashboards and instrument clusters for automakers such as TVS, Honda, Royal Enfield and Ather Energy, will be demerged into a separate entity called Pricol Autotech.

title: India's balance of payments surplus soars to $66.8 billion in H1 FY27 on strong bank deposit inflows
summary: The current account deficit meanwhile widened to $25.8 billion for the first six months of FY27 from $18 billion on account of unfavourable merchandise flows.
